source: Databricks Utilities reference (docs.databricks.com/dev-tools/databricks-utils) and the notebook magic commands Databricks notebooks take (%python, %sql, %scala, %r, %md, %sh, %fs, %run, %pip).

dbutils.data.summarize: Shows a summary table of the DataFrame; the precise flag is ignored.
dbutils.fs.cp: Paths are the attached lakehouse (Files/...) or file: paths on this PC. dbfs:/, /Volumes/ and other bare absolute paths are Databricks storage and are refused by name.
dbutils.fs.head: Same paths as fs.cp.
dbutils.fs.mounts: Returns an empty list: there are no mounts on this PC.
dbutils.fs.mv: Same paths as fs.cp. A folder moves whole, so recurse is not needed.
dbutils.fs.refreshMounts: Does nothing and returns True: there are no mounts on this PC.
dbutils.notebook.entry_point.getDbutils: Gives the notebook's path and your user name for getContext(); the run id is empty.
dbutils.notebook.run: Runs a notebook from this PC's notebooks folder. The timeout and arguments are taken; arguments arrive as widget values.
dbutils.secrets.get: A secret scope is an Azure Key Vault name, read with your own sign-in. Databricks-backed scopes are not reachable.
dbutils.secrets.list: Same scopes as secrets.get. You need the Key Vault Secrets User role.
dbutils.secrets.listScopes: Returns an empty list and says that a scope is a Key Vault name: this PC can't list your vaults.

cells.%sql: Runs on this PC's Spark SQL (DuckDB with Spark's functions).
cells.%sh: Runs as a script on this PC, not on a cluster driver.

line_magics.%run: Runs a notebook from this PC's notebooks folder in the same session.
line_magics.%fs: ls, head, cp, mv, rm, mkdirs and put, with the same paths as dbutils.fs. A drive path (C:\data) is also taken.
line_magics.%pip: Installs into the notebook's own environment on this PC, never the engine's. Your organization's policy can turn installs off.
